reasons: Shows fixed sample medicines instead of real scan results.
Only two of the four sections are visible.

terms.meaning: optical character recognition, the technique of reading text from a photo
a number from 0 to 1 that says how sure the scanner is about a reading

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the review screen
sections.what: Loads the layout pieces, icons, navigation, theme colors and shared UI parts for the review page.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. These are needed to draw the page.
sections.watch_out: The theme and UI are loaded by relative paths, so moving this file will break those links.

sections.name: extractedMeds
sections.title: Sample scanned medicines
sections.what: Three fixed medicines, each with a name, dose, how often to take it, meal timing and a confidence score.
sections.why: Likely reason: placeholder data to show the design before real scanning is connected. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: These are not real results. The confidence numbers are fixed and do not reflect any real reading.

sections.name: OcrReviewScreen (part 1)
sections.title: Scan result banner and medicine cards
sections.what: Shows a green OCR Extraction Complete banner and one card per medicine from the extractedMeds list, with its name, dosage, frequency, meal timing, a confidence percentage, and Edit and Create Reminder buttons. The banner text (Tesseract, 91.7 percent, 420 ms) is typed in and does not come from the scan.
sections.why: Likely reason: a screen where the user checks each scanned medicine before confirming it.
sections.watch_out: The banner text is fixed, so it always reports the same engine and confidence, and the Edit and Create Reminder buttons do nothing yet.

sections.name: OcrReviewScreen (part 2)
sections.title: Sample raw text and action buttons
sections.what: Shows a fixed block of sample prescription text with a doctor, a clinic and three medicines, plus Confirm All and Re-scan buttons. Neither button does anything yet.
sections.why: Likely reason: placeholder content while the real text from the scan is not yet connected to this screen.
sections.watch_out: Someone testing the screen may mistake this sample text for a real scan of someone's prescription.

summary: A review screen for medicines read from a prescription photo. It currently shows a fixed list of sample results, each with a confidence score.
purpose: Lets the user check the scanned medicine names, doses and timing before they are saved.
why: Likely reason: scanned text is not always right, so a person should confirm it. Reason not stated beyond this.
how: Imports the layout pieces and the theme, then shows a fixed list of three medicines with a confidence score each. The rest of the screen is not visible in this packet.
inputs: Fixed sample values in the file.
outputs: A visible review list. Nothing is saved by the visible code.
risks: Shows made-up medicines instead of the real scan result, which could mislead a user about their own prescription.
debug: If the medicines shown do not match the user's scan, check whether the sample list is still in use. Once the scan service is connected, check how its results reach this screen.
